Braided Zopf Loaf

Served at: Berchtoldstag

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 35 min

Zopf is a traditional Swiss braided bread, enjoyed especially on Berchtoldstag, a Swiss holiday celebrated the day after New Year's Day. This soft, slightly sweet bread is perfect for sharing with family and friends during the festive morning meal.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 packet (2 1/4 tsp or 7 g) active dry yeast
  • 1 cup (240 ml) warm milk
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 3 tbsp (45 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 egg yolk (for egg wash)
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) water (for egg wash)

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm milk and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, and salt.
  3. Add the yeast mixture, melted butter, and egg to the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
  4. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  6. Punch down the dough and divide it into three equal parts.
  7. Roll each part into a long rope, about 16 inches (40 cm) long.
  8. Braid the three ropes together, pinching the ends to seal and tucking them under the loaf.
  9. Place the braided loaf on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and cover with a towel; let it rise for another 30 minutes.
  10. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  11. Mix the egg yolk with water and brush the egg wash over the loaf to give it a shiny crust.
  12. Bake the loaf for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped.
  13. Remove from oven and let cool on a wire rack before slicing.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half the milk with cream.
  • Add a teaspoon of vanilla extract or lemon zest to the dough for a subtle aroma.
  • Serve fresh with butter and jam for a traditional Berchtoldstag breakfast.
